rule identifier: branches 1 and 3 are order-dependent (shared first bytes; ordered choice is decisive)

source:
# Port of lib/pubid/adobe/parser.rb: tech notes (Adobe TN 5014, legacy
# "Adobe Technical Note #5014", ATN5014, bare 5014) and publications
# (adobe-glyph-list, adobe-japan1-7 with the version split tried first).
#
# Edition 2: every reference inside a captured body is inlined to raw
# terms (a rule reference materializes as a named node in the edition-2
# tree, so only a raw capture binds a scalar span). The prefix spellings
# and slug shapes live inline below; the wrapper captures (tech_note,
# tech_note_bare, publication_version) keep the v1 tree shape and the
# bindings name their scalar leaves.

grammar PubidAdobe version "0.1.0" edition 2 {

  # Capture precedence: (*rep) as name wraps the whole repetition, so a
  # digit run joins to one string instead of re-keying every character;
  # slug is captured exactly once (the bare form) or as a sibling of
  # version inside the publication_version capture. The three prefix
  # spellings are inlined longest-first (ordered choice is decisive).
  tech_note = {
    (
      ( "Adobe" " " "TN" [" "]
        / "Adobe" " " "Technical" " " "Note" [[" "] ["#"] [" "]]
        / "ATN" [" "] )
      (1*%x30-39) as number
      [("." (1*(%x41-5A / %x61-7A / %x30-39 / %x5F)) as slug)]
    ) as tech_note
  }
  # The bare form captures the digit run as one span: the builder
  # stringifies the :tech_note_bare value AS the number (no nested read),
  # so an inner capture here would render the hash, not the digits.
  bare_number = (1*%x30-39) as tech_note_bare
  # Slug text: a lower-case lead segment, then dash-joined segments.
  publication_with_version = {
    (
      ( 1*%x61-7A *(%x61-7A / %x30-39)
        *("-" 1*%x61-7A *(%x61-7A / %x30-39)) ) as slug
      "-"
      (1*%x30-39) as version
    ) as publication_version
  }
  slug_inner = {
    ( 1*%x61-7A *(%x61-7A / %x30-39)
      *("-" 1*%x61-7A *(%x61-7A / %x30-39)) ) as slug
  }
  publication_slug_or_version = publication_with_version / slug_inner
  publication = ["Adobe Publication "] publication_slug_or_version
  identifier = tech_note / bare_number / publication

  entry identifier: identifier

  test {
    accept "Adobe TN 15"
    accept "ATN 30"
    accept "Adobe Technical Note #12"
    reject "###"
  }

  bindings identifier {
    # The builder dispatches on the wrapper keys and reads the leaves from
    # inside them (adobe/builder.rb build_tech_note / build_publication_version),
    # so the wrappers bind uncast — the nested hash the builder expects. The
    # scalar bindings carry the same leaves flat for typed consumers.
    tech_note -> tech_note (raw)
    tech_note_bare -> tech_note_bare (string)
    publication_version -> publication_version (raw)
    number -> number (string)
    slug -> slug (string)
    version -> version (string)
  }
}
